extracted.description: Compute the proportion of fraud reporters who lost between $1 and $500 (inclusive bounds as stated) in 2024, expressed as a single numeric ratio.
The analysis population is restricted to fraud reporters with reports occurring in calendar year 2024; the $1-$500 loss criterion applies only to the numerator subset.
The computed proportion must be mathematically valid and rounded to exactly 3 decimal places.
The completeness of the 2024 fraud reporter population must be supported by audit evidence.

stored.description: Compute the proportion of fraud reporters who lost between $1 and $500 (inclusive bounds as stated) in 2024, expressed as a single numeric ratio.
acceptanceCriteria: Result is a single numeric value representing a ratio, not a count or percentage with a % sign
Numerator counts fraud reporters in 2024 whose reported loss amount falls within the $1-$500 range
Denominator counts all fraud reporters in 2024 regardless of loss amount
Ratio is computed as numerator divided by denominator from the same 2024 population

assertions.description: Compute the proportion of fraud reporters who lost between $1 and $500 (inclusive bounds as stated) in 2024, expressed as a single numeric ratio.

stored.description: The analysis population is restricted to fraud reporters with reports occurring in calendar year 2024; the $1-$500 loss criterion applies only to the numerator subset.
acceptanceCriteria: Both numerator and denominator are limited to fraud reports dated within calendar year 2024 (no other years included)
The $1-$500 loss filter is applied to the numerator but not to the denominator
Boundary values $1 and $500 are handled consistently and the applied boundary inclusion/exclusion is auditable

assertions.description: The analysis population is restricted to fraud reporters with reports occurring in calendar year 2024; the $1-$500 loss criterion applies only to the numerator subset.

stored.description: The computed proportion must be mathematically valid and rounded to exactly 3 decimal places.
acceptanceCriteria: Denominator is greater than zero; a zero denominator is flagged as a failure rather than returned as a result
Final value is rounded (not truncated) to exactly 3 decimal places
Numerator is less than or equal to denominator, confirming the subset relationship

assertions.description: The computed proportion must be mathematically valid and rounded to exactly 3 decimal places.

stored.description: The completeness of the 2024 fraud reporter population must be supported by audit evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit evidence shows the denominator record count and the numerator record count used in the calculation
Records excluded from the 2024 population (e.g., null or out-of-range loss amounts in the denominator) are accounted for and their treatment is documented
The reported final answer is reproducible from the recorded numerator and denominator counts after rounding

assertions.description: The completeness of the 2024 fraud reporter population must be supported by audit evidence.
